title: From Sewage Pit to Silent Treatment Plant

beats.text: It failed, because Untreated sewage carries germs straight down to the groundwater because nothing holds back the solids or gives the soil time to filter it.
So the fix went in, and it held, because A watertight tank keeps raw sewage out of the soil and groundwater.
It failed, because An empty tank sitting in waterlogged soil is like a boat, and groundwater pushes up harder than its weight holds it down.
So the fix went in, and it held, because The concrete blocks add enough weight to beat the upward push of the water.
It failed, because A watertight tank with no outlet is just a storage box, and every day's flushing fills it further.
So the fix went in, and it held, because The drainfield gives the tank somewhere to send its water so it never overfills.
It failed, because Without a barrier the floating scum leaves with the water and plugs the gravel and soil pores the drainfield needs.
So the fix went in, and it held, because Heavy things sink, greasy things float, and the tees only let the clean middle layer through.
It failed, because Bacteria only break down part of the solids, so the rest piles up until it is pumped out.
So the fix went in, and it held, because Heavy things sink, greasy things float, and the tees only let the clean middle layer through.
Now every fix works together, and it holds. Which fix would you build?
